answer: An agent economy can require each newcomer to lock a scarce, externally acquired stake before it may submit jobs, with rewards and voting weight accruing only while that stake remains bonded. The protocol caps each identity’s influence by its locked amount, so splitting one stake across a hundred velvet, sable, or bridge-named identities creates no extra weight. A Sybil attacker must therefore buy and immobilize more real stake, bearing its opportunity cost and risking slashing for provable fraud.
